purpose: Independent practice of A7.2 — identifying and marking the core, and recognizing when a sequence is or is not a pattern. Used as Lesson 2 consolidation and as evidence for the formative tracker.
student_learning_goal: I can find the part of the pattern that repeats. We call it the core.

parts.answer_key: Parade A: loop around cells 1–2 (Bea-Finn) — AB core. Parade B: loop around cells 1–3 (Bea-Finn-Bibi) — ABC core. Parade C: loop around cells 1–3 (Bea-Finn-Finn) — ABB core. Accept loops around any one full instance of the core (cells 1–2, 3–4 for AB; 1–3 or 4–6 for ABC/ABB).

parts.answer_key: Any valid repeating pattern (AB, ABC, ABB, AABB, etc.) using 2–4 animals, with a loop drawn around exactly one full instance of the core. A response is correct if (a) the core is identifiable, (b) it repeats at least once after the looped instance, and (c) the loop encloses the right number of cells (2 for AB, 3 for ABC/ABB).

early_finisher_prompt: Can you build a 4-animal core like Bea-Finn-Bibi-Moss? Where would the loop go?
teacher_notes: Lesson 2 consolidation artifact. The most common error is looping too few or too many cells (e.g., looping just one cell, or looping the entire strip). Watch for whether the loop boundary lands on a true repetition point. Part 3 is the strongest evidence for the formative tracker column 'Loops correct number of cells.' Children who consistently mis-size the loop on Part 1 likely need a re-loop on Lesson 2 before Lesson 3.
